inline_comments.comment:
The inner alternation arms contain unnecessary capturing groups: `"([^"\\]|\\.)*"` and `'([^'\\]|\\.)*'`. Since Langium passes the full token text to the value converter (not individual capture groups), these groups capture nothing useful and add noise. Replace them with non-capturing groups to match the style of the rest of the codebase:

```langium
terminal ARCH_TITLE: /\[(?:"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"|'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'|[\w ]+)\]/;
```

After `expect(service).toBeDefined()`, TypeScript's type for `service` is not narrowed, so `service?.title` uses optional chaining unnecessarily. Per project convention, avoid `?.` on values already guarded — use `assert(service !== undefined)` (imported from `vitest`) to narrow the type, then access `service.title` unconditionally. The same pattern applies on lines 113, 126, 138.

None of the new test cases exercise the primary practical benefit of quoted strings: labels that contain characters outside the `[\w ]` set (e.g. hyphens, dots, slashes, commas). A test like `service db(database)["API v2.0"]` expecting `API v2.0` would directly demonstrate why quoted strings are needed beyond unquoted ones. Without such a test, the regression coverage for the reported issue is incomplete.

general_comments.comment: The root cause of all the correctness issues here is that the value converter treats quote characters as pure syntax markers that should always be removed, rather than as optional delimiters that wrap — but are not part of — the label text. The Langium terminal regex correctly distinguishes quoted from unquoted forms at the grammar level, but the converter then discards that structural information and applies a flat global strip. The fix should model the two forms explicitly: (1) strip `[` and `]` from the ends, (2) if what remains is delimited by a matched quote pair, slice off exactly those two characters. This mirrors how every other string-terminal value converter in Langium-based parsers works and is consistent with the project rule 'strip only the necessary wrapper characters'.

The changeset level of `patch` is appropriate for a bug fix. However, the changeset message `fix: Allow quoted string labels in architecture-beta diagrams` could be more precise about what was broken (a syntax error when the `["..."]` form was used) to help readers scanning the changelog understand the concrete behaviour change.
